content_paraphrased: Use and interpret algebraic notation: ab, 3y, a², a³, a²b, a/b, coefficients as fractions not decimals, brackets
teaching: Products, repeated sums, powers, division as a fraction, expressions from words; decimal coefficients flagged
independent_evidence: algebra.notation (form: no × or ÷ signs, fractions not decimals)

content_paraphrased: Substitute numerical values into formulae and expressions, including scientific formulae
teaching: Positive and negative values, powers, v = u + at, s = ut + ½at², E = ½mv², temperature conversion; finding a non-subject value
gap: Calculator use not enforced or practised

content_paraphrased: Understand and use the vocabulary of expressions, equations, formulae, identities, inequalities, terms and factors
teaching: Naming statements; counting terms; factors of a term; identity vs equation

content_paraphrased: Simplify and manipulate algebraic expressions (including surds; Higher: algebraic fractions): collect like terms, single brackets, common factors, products of binomials, factorise x² + bx + c including difference of two squares, laws of indices
higher_only_part: Higher: algebraic fractions; products of two or more binomials; factorising ax² + bx + c
teaching: Collecting like terms; index laws with coefficients; expanding and factorising single brackets; double brackets; x² + bx + c and difference of two squares; Higher: three binomials and ax² + bx + c

gap: Algebraic fractions (Higher) and algebraic surd expressions not built; negative and fractional algebraic indices not practised

content_paraphrased: Understand and use standard mathematical formulae; rearrange formulae to change the subject
teaching: Finding unknowns from formulae; one- and two-step rearranging; fractions, squares and the subject appearing twice
gap: Rearrangements needing a square root are not marked (typed roots of expressions not supported)

content_paraphrased: Know the difference between an equation and an identity; argue mathematically to show expressions are equivalent; construct arguments (Higher: and proofs)
gap: Show-that arguments and proofs are not marked

content_paraphrased: Interpret simple expressions as functions with inputs and outputs (Higher: inverse and composite functions, formal notation)
higher_only_part: Higher: inverse function; composite function; function notation
teaching: Expression and reverse machines in investigations
gap: Function notation, inverse and composite functions not built

content_paraphrased: Work with coordinates in all four quadrants
Plot straight-line graphs; use y = mx + c to identify parallel lines; equation of a line through two points or one point with a gradient
Identify and interpret gradients and intercepts of linear functions graphically and algebraically
Identify and interpret roots, intercepts and turning points of quadratic functions graphically; deduce roots algebraically
higher_only_part: Higher: turning points by completing the square
teaching: Roots as x-axis crossings (investigation and worked examples); Higher: turning point by completing the square
gap: Reading roots, intercepts and turning points from plotted graphs is not marked; graph strand still to build

content_paraphrased: Recognise, sketch and interpret graphs of linear, quadratic, simple cubic and reciprocal functions
higher_only_part: Higher: exponential y = kˣ and trigonometric graphs

content_paraphrased: Sketch translations and reflections of a given function
Plot and interpret graphs, including reciprocal graphs and non-standard functions in real contexts (kinematics)
Calculate or estimate gradients of graphs and areas under graphs; interpret in context (no calculus)
Equation of a circle with centre at the origin; tangent to a circle at a given point
Solve linear equations in one unknown algebraically, including unknown on both sides; find approximate solutions using a graph
teaching: One- and two-step equations, negatives and fraction answers, fractions in equations, brackets, unknown on both sides
independent_evidence: algebra.solve; algebra.solve-both-sides (answers accepted as x = …, fractions or decimals)

content_paraphrased: Solve quadratic equations by factorising; approximate solutions from a graph
higher_only_part: Higher: requiring rearrangement; completing the square; quadratic formula
teaching: Solving by factorising, difference of two squares, common factor; Higher: rearrangement first, ax² + bx + c, completing the square, the quadratic formula to 2 d.p.
gap: Approximate solutions from a graph not marked; exact surd solutions by completing the square not asked

content_paraphrased: Solve two simultaneous equations (linear/linear) algebraically; approximate solutions from a graph
teaching: Elimination with and without multiplying; graphs show the intersection; Higher: linear/quadratic (parabola and circle)
gap: Approximate solutions from drawn graphs not marked; practice solutions are whole numbers

content_paraphrased: Find approximate solutions to equations numerically using iteration
Translate situations into expressions or formulae; derive an equation (or two simultaneous equations), solve and interpret
teaching: Expressions from words; forming and solving linear equations; forming simultaneous equations from prices and a line through two points
gap: Interpretation of solutions is implicit; contexts are limited to a few templates

content_paraphrased: Solve linear inequalities in one variable; represent the solution set on a number line
higher_only_part: Higher: two variables; quadratic inequalities; set notation; graphs
teaching: Number-line representation; solving linear inequalities including dividing by a negative and double inequalities; integer solutions; Higher: quadratic inequalities
gap: Higher: inequalities in two variables, regions on a graph and set notation not built; number lines drawn only in the investigation

content_paraphrased: Generate terms of a sequence from a term-to-term or position-to-term rule
teaching: Term-to-term and position-to-term rules; deciding whether a number is a term

higher_only_part: Higher: r a surd; other sequences

gap: Higher: geometric sequences with a surd ratio and other sequences not practised

teaching: Linear nth term (increasing and decreasing) and using it; Higher: quadratic nth term
